messages:
emma: FYI apiserver tail latency (p99) jumping in southamerica1 since ~16:40. etcd leader churned 3 times between 1902468030-1902468090, controller-manager queues ballooning. noticed a spike in retransmits on ctrl-plane links.
rob: seeing same. RTT skewed and some peers reporting TCP RTOs. provisioning-controller logs show repeated "AttachVolume timed out" + GPU allocation retries. backlog at ~140 pending GPU pods.
sanjay: any network noise from peering?
emma: ran a short capture on ctrl-03 -> ctrl-02, dropping sample below. looks like fragmentation + dup acks.
```
16:41:10.100 IP ctrl-03 > ctrl-02: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1380], length 0
16:41:10.305 IP ctrl-02 > ctrl-03: frag-needed icmp (mtu 1400)
16:41:10.506 IP ctrl-03 > ctrl-02: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1380], length 0
16:41:10.709 IP ctrl-03 > ctrl-02: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 (retransmit)
```
rob: that frag-needed ICMP implies MTU mismatch somewhere in the corridor. ICMPs being filtered could cause long tail retransmits and trigger raft election timeouts.
ops-bot: alert: etcd_election_count increased by 3 in 5m in southamerica1 at 1902468075.
sanjay: quick mitigation idea: divert a portion of NEW GPU claims to us-west1 (best-effort batch jobs only) and reduce controller-manager parallelism to shrink reconciliation fan-out while infra traces the path.
emma: agree. aim to divert ~25% new claims and keep current pods alone. rob, can you apply placement rule + controller patch?
rob: applying now. placement rule: `prov.redwood/placement-preference=us-west1:25%` via provisioner annotation. controller patch: `kubectl -n kube-system patch deploy kube-controller-manager -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-controller-manager","args":["--concurrent-deployment-syncs=2","--concurrent-replicaset-syncs=1","--concurrent-service-syncs=1"]}]}}}}'`
ops-bot: placement override `gpu-uswest-canary` created by rob at 1902468160. controller-manager patch applied at 1902468175.
emma: metrics: apiserver_p99 fell from 2.2s -> 640ms within 4m. etcd leader flips stopped. pending GPU pods reduced from 140 -> 48 in 7m. good sign.
sanjay: cost impact estimate: moving 35 GPUs to us-west1 (approx 25% of new claims) adds ~0.12$/GPU-hr (spot premium + egress). ~35 * 0.12 = 4.2$/hr -> ~100$/day, plus some scheduling overhead. I'll record to COST-7332.
infra-net: we see a transient path MTU regression on the southamerica1 peering fabric coinciding with a router OS update. rolling back the patch now and adding icmp-unreachable monitoring. opened NET-4219 for long-term guardrails.
rob: infra-net, can you also confirm whether ICMP:frag-needed was rate-limited? that would explain retransmit pileup.
infra-net: confirmed some ICMPs were rate-limited by an intermediate appliance during the update. rollback and ICMP policy change in progress. ETA 20m.
ops-bot: NET-4219 created and linked to INF-9123 at 1902468210.
emma: plan for next 30m: 1) keep canary placement active for new claims, 2) maintain lower controller concurrency, 3) monitor apiserver_p99, etcd_elections, controller_queue_depth, and GPU pending count. if stable after 30m, gradually return placement to normal.
sanjay: also adding a short-term admission webhook to mark non-critical GPU pods as `best-effort` so provisioner picks fallback (low friction). will coordinate with platform teams.
rob: once infra confirms ICMP fix, i'll run a controlled reenable: remove placement override, revert controller args back to defaults in staged steps.
emma: thanks team. i'll draft incident notes, include tcpdump snippets and cost calc. leaving canary for 25m. :thumbsup:
